items.text: Identify the correct relative pronouns for people, things, and time.
Master vocabulary for emergencies and heroic actions.
Combine complex sentences to describe historical and fictional heroes.

slides.title: HERO OR NOT?
slides.question: Which of these people are REAL heroes? Why?

strategy_items.text: Read the story of Nasreddin Hodja.
Choose the correct relative pronouns. (Workbook Page 37)

slides.title: NASREDDIN'S STORY
slides.text: Nasreddin Hodja was a wise man and storyteller who / which lived in the 13th century. He's famous because there are thousands of stories where / which he's a kind of comic hero. In one story, he searches for a ring which / who he had lost in his house. After searching briefly inside the house, where / which he's sure the ring is, he goes to look outside.

slides.title: NASREDDIN'S STORY
slides.text: Nasreddin answers, 'Because this is when / where the light is the best!' Why do we call someone which / who makes such a silly mistake a hero? Because even at times who / when he makes silly mistakes, he believes in himself. Comic heroes manage to show us the funny side of situations which / where make most people angry or upset.

strategy_items.text: Match the emergency phrases (1-5) to their definitions (a-e).
[HIGHLIGHT: Defining]: Necessary info. No commas! (e.g., The man who lived next door.)
[HIGHLIGHT: Non-defining]: Extra info. Use commas! (e.g., Rosa Parks, who was brave, sat down.)
[HIGHLIGHT: Omission]: You can hide the pronoun in [HIGHLIGHT: Defining] clauses only.
Combine the sentences using non-defining relative clauses.
Remember: Use commas for extra information!

slides.title: ROSA PARKS
slides.question: Rosa Parks refused to give up her seat. She is known as 'the first lady of civil rights'.
slides.answer: Rosa Parks, [HIGHLIGHT: who is known as 'the first lady of civil rights'], refused to give up her seat.
slides.explanation: She is a symbol of courage and equality.

slides.title: SHAKESPEARE
slides.question: Shakespeare is one of the world's most famous playwrights. His plays influenced the English language.
slides.answer: Shakespeare, [HIGHLIGHT: whose plays influenced the English language], is a world-famous playwright.
slides.explanation: His work is still studied globally today.

slides.title: MARIE CURIE
slides.question: Marie Curie was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize. She won the prize in 1903.
slides.answer: Marie Curie, [HIGHLIGHT: who won the Nobel Prize in 1903], was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize.

slides.title: My Real-Life Hero
slides.subtitle: Your turn to describe a hero

strategy_items.text: Who is a hero in your life? Describe them.
Use at least three relative clauses (who, which, where, when, or whose).
Is it their courage, intelligence, or kindness?
What are the different ways someone can be a hero?
Is being a hero about what you DO or who you ARE?
